 US War on Iran Drives UK Inflation to 3.6% As Petrol, Diesel Prices Surge 
 November, 18, 2026 - 14:20 
 Economy news 
 TEHRAN (Tasnim) – UK inflation climbed to 3.6% in October as soaring petrol and diesel prices increased the cost of living, with the economic fallout from the US war on Iran continuing to drive up energy prices and deepen inflationary pressures. 
 Economy 
 The annual inflation rate rose from 3.5% in September to 3.6% in October, according to figures released by the Office for National Statistics (ONS), reflecting the growing impact of US aggression against Iran and the resulting disruption to global energy markets.
 Rising oil prices have also increased the cost of raw materials and manufactured goods, adding to economic pressures on British businesses and households.
 The impact has been particularly evident in fuel prices, with petrol rising by 5.2 pence per liter between September and October to an average of 174.7 pence per liter, its highest level since August 2022.
 Diesel prices climbed to an average of 199.5 pence per liter in October, marking their highest level since records began 30 years ago.
 Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the ONS, said fuel prices were "once again a major contributor" to the increase in inflation in October.
 He added on Wednesday: "Annual costs of both raw materials and goods leaving factories continue to climb, driven by higher crude oil and petrol prices, respectively."
 The continued rise in energy costs is also threatening to increase the prices of food and other essential goods as businesses transfer higher production and transportation expenses to consumers.
 Although the Bank of England said earlier this month there was "limited evidence" that businesses were passing all additional costs on to customers, some companies have absorbed the increases at the expense of their profit margins.
 Meanwhile, the inflationary pressures have prompted the Bank of England to raise interest rates for the first time in three years, increasing the rate from 3.75% to 4% in an attempt to contain rising prices.
 The central bank has warned that another interest rate increase could be necessary unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, raising the prospect of further financial pressure on British households and businesses.
 The latest figures highlight the wider economic consequences of the US war on Iran, as Washington's military aggression and escalating confrontation in the region contribute to instability in global energy markets and expose Western economies to mounting economic costs.
 The ONS also reported that price inflation in restaurants and cafes slowed in October, while average hotel prices declined.
